name: Chicken Mousse
description: Historical recipe from The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: breast of a raw chicken pounded and forced through a purée strainer
ingredients.originalText: 1/2 breast of a raw chicken pounded and forced through a purée strainer

ingredients.name: salt, pepper, and cayenne to taste
ingredients.originalText: salt, pepper, and cayenne to taste

ingredients.name: cooked white chicken meat rubbed through a sieve
ingredients.originalText: 3/4 cup cooked white chicken meat rubbed through a sieve

ingredients.name: heavy cream beaten until stiff
ingredients.originalText: 1/2 cup heavy cream beaten until stiff

instructions.text: Make a chicken force-meat of pounded raw chicken breast forced through a purée strainer, white of one egg slightly beaten, one-half cup heavy cream, and salt, pepper, and cayenne to taste
Add cooked white chicken meat rubbed through a sieve, white of an egg slightly beaten, and one-half cup heavy cream beaten until stiff
Decorate a buttered mould with truffles
Turn in mixture, set in pan of hot water, cover with buttered paper, and bake until firm
Remove to platter and pour around Cream or Béchamel Sauce

source.author: Fannie Merritt Farmer
source.originalInstructions:
1. Make a chicken force-meat of pounded raw chicken breast forced through a purée strainer, white of one egg slightly beaten, one-half cup heavy cream, and salt, pepper, and cayenne to taste
2. Add cooked white chicken meat rubbed through a sieve, white of an egg slightly beaten, and one-half cup heavy cream beaten until stiff
3. Decorate a buttered mould with truffles
4. Turn in mixture, set in pan of hot water, cover with buttered paper, and bake until firm
5. Remove to platter and pour around Cream or Béchamel Sauce
